Count reads in files within a directory

Source: R/vtamR_fun.R
count_reads_in_dir.Rd

Count the number of sequences in FASTA or FASTQ files, or the number of lines in other file types, for all files in a directory matching a given pattern.

Usage

count_reads_in_dir(
  dir,
  pattern = ".",
  file_type = "fasta",
  outfile = NULL,
  chunk_lines = 1e+05,
  fast_count = TRUE,
  sep = ",",
  quiet = T
)

Arguments

dir

Character string: path to the input directory.

pattern

Regular expression: pattern used to select files in the directory. Only files whose names match the pattern are processed.

file_type

Character string specifying file type: "fasta" or "fastq". For any other value, the function returns the number of lines in each file.

outfile

Character string: output CSV file name. If NULL, no file is written.

chunk_lines

Integer specifying the maximum number of lines to read at a time when using the chunk-based counting method. Defaults to 1e5. Passed to count_reads().

fast_count

Logical value controlling the counting method. When TRUE on Linux-like systems, shell commands are used for faster counting. When FALSE, the chunk-based R implementation is used. Passed to count_reads().

sep

Field separator character in input and output CSV files.

quiet

Logical: if TRUE, suppress informational messages and show only warnings or errors.

Value

Data frame with two columns: filename, read_count.

Details

This function is optimized for Linux-like systems and may be slower on Windows for large files. It supports both gz-compressed and uncompressed files (ZIP archives are not supported).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
count_reads_in_dir(dir = "out", pattern = "\\.fastq", file_type = "fastq")
count_reads_in_dir(dir = "out", pattern = "^mfzr", file_type = "fasta")
} # }
